description: Na₆Si₂Se₇ crystallizes in the monoclinic C2/c space group. There are four inequivalent Na¹⁺ sites. In the first Na¹⁺ site, Na¹⁺ is bonded in a distorted see-saw-like geometry to four Se²⁻ atoms. There are two shorter (2.82 Å) and two longer (2.89 Å) Na-Se bond lengths. In the second Na¹⁺ site, Na¹⁺ is bonded to six Se²⁻ atoms to form NaSe₆ octahedra that share corners with two equivalent NaSe₆ octahedra, corners with two equivalent SiSe₄ tetrahedra, edges with four equivalent NaSe₆ octahedra, and edges with two equivalent SiSe₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles are 5°. There are a spread of Na-Se bond distances ranging from 2.86-3.23 Å. In the third Na¹⁺ site, Na¹⁺ is bonded to six Se²⁻ atoms to form distorted NaSe₆ octahedra that share corners with two NaSe₆ octahedra,  a cornercorner with one SiSe₄ tetrahedra, edges with four NaSe₆ octahedra, and edges with three equivalent SiSe₄ tetrahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 5-40°. There are a spread of Na-Se bond distances ranging from 2.96-3.47 Å. In the fourth Na¹⁺ site, Na¹⁺ is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to six Se²⁻ atoms. There are a spread of Na-Se bond distances ranging from 2.95-3.55 Å. Si⁴⁺ is bonded to four Se²⁻ atoms to form SiSe₄ tetrahedra that share corners with two NaSe₆ octahedra,  a cornercorner with one SiSe₄ tetrahedra, and edges with four NaSe₆ octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 19-59°. There are a spread of Si-Se bond distances ranging from 2.25-2.33 Å. There are four inequivalent Se²⁻ sites. In the first Se²⁻ site, Se²⁻ is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to four Na¹⁺ and two equivalent Si⁴⁺ atoms. In the second Se²⁻ site, Se²⁻ is bonded to five Na¹⁺ and one Si⁴⁺ atom to form a mixture of distorted corner and edge-sharing SeNa₅Si octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 0-78°. In the third Se²⁻ site, Se²⁻ is bonded to five Na¹⁺ and one Si⁴⁺ atom to form a mixture of corner and edge-sharing SeNa₅Si octahedra. The corner-sharing octahedral tilt angles range from 0-4°. In the fourth Se²⁻ site, Se²⁻ is bonded in a 6-coordinate geometry to five Na¹⁺ and one Si⁴⁺ atom.
